messages:
tariq: Heads-up — spotted a reproducible flash where the console shows another org's insights card for ~3s when rapidly switching projects. Seen it twice in prod during the rollout window. :eyes:

maya: ugh. can you repro reliably? steps?

tariq: yes — steps: 1) open org A dashboard, 2) hit quick-switch to org B fast (keyboard), 3) click Insights tab immediately. sometimes the card payload contains org_id=B but owner_id/A rows remain.

sam: do you have an example payload? logs?

tariq: pasted a snippet from edge logs (sanitized):
```
INFO router req_id=abc123 path=/api/insights headers={"X-Org-ID":"B","X-Request-Source":"console"} backend=insights-db shard=shard-3 route=fastprefetch
INFO prefetchtask task_id=pt-987 src_org=A cache_hit=false returned_rows=5
```

maya: whoa — header says B but prefetchtask says src_org=A. that smells like a context swap in the connector queue.

liam: possible timeline: console sends two rapid requests (prefetch + render). router picks different backend instances that have stale in-memory per-connection tenant tag. older instances still had `currentOrg=A` sticky on connection.

sam: are we leaking state via long-lived connections? we did recently change the connector pool to keep gRPC channels alive across tenants for perf.

maya: that change was rolled out last week for the fastprefetch route.

tariq: repro reliably on canary by toggling `FastPrefetch=true` in my console account and hammering quick-switch. see attached trace id abc123.

liam: quick mitigation: failfast any request where `X-Org-ID` != connection.affinity_org on router side. we can short-circuit and re-establish a fresh connection. downside: perf hit for cross-org spiky flows.

sam: and we should also tag telemetry for these mismatch events so we can measure frequency. currently telemetry attributes only include `route` and `shard`, no `header_mismatch` flag.

maya: agree. add `org_affinity_mismatch=true` to spans when we detect this. that'll help quantify.

deploy-bot: deploy started: router/connector-pool v2.14 -> canary (10%) by liam at 2025-03-18T15:30:00Z

liam: proposed fix:
- enforce per-request tenant stamp on connector checkout (cheap)
- if mismatch, increment metric `connector.org_mismatch` and increment counter for route
- failfast path to close channel and retry once
- add a rollout flag `connector.checkout.strict_org_check` default=false for gradual enable

sam: code stub for strict check: 
```go
// on checkout
if cfg.StrictOrgCheck && conn.AffinityOrg != req.Headers.Get("X-Org-ID") {
    metrics.Inc("connector.org_mismatch")
    conn.Close() // drop sticky state
    return ErrRetryOnNewConn
}
```

maya: also need to make dashboards show this metric per-customer so support can filter for affected orgs. right now metrics are aggregated by route only.

tariq: small UX ask: when this happens, from console let's surface a subtle toast: "Content loading — validating workspace" instead of showing card from previous workspace. less alarming for customers.

liam: good idea. low-risk. we can set a feature flag behind `ui.show_affinity_revalidate_toast` for a canary cohort.

sam: will open PR for the router change + metric & circuit. planning to cut a patch release tomorrow.

maya: ops: can you add a short-running alert? e.g., if `connector.org_mismatch` > 5/min in prod, page eng-platform on-call. we should not spam during rollout — make it P2 with 15m aggregation.

tariq: pinging support so they can correlate support tickets: @support-team — we may get a flurry of "wrong org" reports during canary.

liam: timeline: patch -> canary 10% -> monitor `connector.org_mismatch` and `console.ui.toast_shown` -> enable strict check cluster-wide after 24h with no regressions.

sam: note: also audit any other services that use long-lived channels (search, reports) — they might have same issue. I'll make a checklist.

maya: thanks everyone. will update the rollout doc and add the telemetry dashboard link: https://internal.redwood/observability/dashboards/affinity-mismatch

tariq: repro script for QA (curl):
```bash
# quick switch then immediate insights fetch
curl -H "X-Org-ID: A" https://console.redwood/api/switch -k
# then immediately
curl -H "X-Org-ID: B" https://console.redwood/api/insights -k -v
```

sam: great, that should do it. leaving a note to add a migration test that creates rapid interleaved requests across orgs. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy complete: router/connector-pool v2.14 -> canary (10%) by liam at 2025-03-18T15:37:40Z

maya: monitoring looks quiet so far, mismatch rate low but visible on canary nodes. thanks for the quick turnaround. :sparkles:
